title: Scientists Report Blood Traces in a 115-Million-Year-Old Dinosaur Bone
paragraphs: Scientists from Curtin University in Australia found signs of blood in a dinosaur bone. The dinosaur was called Aratasaurus. It lived about 115 million years ago in the northeast of Brazil.

Inside the bone, the team saw many tiny red blood cells. They also found a chemical called heme, which carries oxygen in blood. The team found parts of collagen too. Collagen is a protein that gives strength to bones.
The researchers think a mineral kept the cells safe for millions of years. They also think the dinosaur was buried very fast. The leader of the team called it a landmark discovery.

questions.a: A chemical that carries oxygen in blood.

questions.q: Why did the cells stay safe?
questions.a: A mineral probably kept them safe.
